new_statements.quote: p.353: "Históricamente, es interesante ver que, en su época, el chiriguano, que tiene el acento llano en las palabras, conservaba todavía la /h/ intervocálica en todos los casos etimológicos [...] Hoy en día, los simba han eliminado la /h/ más radicalmente que los ava." — p.347: "Se distinguen tres dialectos principales, el ava, o ava-guaraní, el chané y el izoceño. El dialecto ava se subdivide en el ava propiamente dicho, hablado más al Norte, en la zona del Gran Kaipependi, Camiri, Charagua, Lagunillas, Gutiérrez, y el simba 'trenza', que se habla en la parte meridional, es decir entre Cuevo, Villamontes, Ingre, Igüembe y Tentayapi."
new_statements.translation: p.353: "Historically, it is interesting to see that, in his [León de Santiago's] time, Chiriguano, which has paroxytone (penultimate) word stress, still preserved intervocalic /h/ in all etymological cases [...] Today the Simba have eliminated /h/ more radically than the Ava." — p.347: "Three main dialects are distinguished: Ava (Ava-Guaraní), Chané and Izoceño. The Ava dialect subdivides into Ava proper, spoken further north (Gran Kaipependi, Camiri, Charagua, Lagunillas, Gutiérrez), and Simba 'braid', spoken in the southern part, i.e. between Cuevo, Villamontes, Ingre, Igüembe and Tentayapi."

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is 'llano' (paroxytone): it falls on the penultimate syllable of the word, in contrast to the final stress of Paraguayan Guaraní. Morando 2021:174 (held by the project, same folder) states it explicitly for the whole Chiriguano complex including the Simba: 'el acento llano o paroxítono, es decir, aplicado siempre en la penúltima sílaba de una palabra' (citing Dietrich 1986: 58).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Dietrich 2005:356: suffixes treated as unaccented units let stress rest on the last syllable of the preceding lexeme ('como sucede con tantos otros sufijos del chiriguano'); Morando 2021 (Los nombres de la máquina, pp.195-196, held under east2555): Spanish loans such as kamiö 'camión', kerosë 'kerosene' keep Spanish final stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (Dietrich: 'el acento llano en las palabras'; Morando: 'penúltima sílaba de una palabra'). Both statements are about Chiriguano/guaraní chaqueño as a whole; no source gives Simba-specific data on stress, though Dietrich cites Simba data on /h/ in the same paragraph and Morando names simbas among the speaker groups covered.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement is for the Chiriguano / guaraní chaqueño complex as a whole, not for Simba alone. Dietrich 2005:347 classifies simba as the southern sub-dialect of the ava dialect of Chiriguano (= Eastern Bolivian Guaraní, east2555 [gui]); the gnw/gui split is an Ethnologue/SIL one. The same two files already carry the east2555 statement, so the catalog should treat west2640 as covered by the same lineage (one source, two ISO codes) rather than as an independent data point; Morando 2021:174 explicitly names 'simbas' among the groups whose language has penultimate stress. Simba-specific phonology exists only in Gustafson 2014 (print) and possibly Dietrich 1986.
